summary: This article explains why China built and rebuilt the Great Wall over two thousand years, what it was made of, how soldiers used its towers to send signals, and the myth about seeing it from the Moon.
introduce: Draw a simple cause → effect arrow on the board and ask students for an everyday example, such as “I did not sleep, so I felt tired.” Tell them that while reading “The Great Wall of China” they will find at least two cause-and-effect links.

keyTerms.def: moving from place to place instead of living in one spot
to enter a place by force in order to attack or take it
a family of rulers who lead a country for a long time

challengeTerms.def: a wall, tower, or other structure built to defend a place
the edge of a country, where it meets another land
to force someone to work or serve, especially for the government

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that the Great Wall was worth all the work it took to build? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how the people who built and guarded the Great Wall helped protect China.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review nomadic, invade, and dynasty, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use fortification, frontier, and conscript in a short paragraph that explains one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
